questions.q: What are the main features of a perfectly competitive market?
answer: A perfectly competitive market is an ideal form of market that has several defining features.

answer.text: There are a very large number of buyers and sellers, each so small in relation to the whole market that no single one can influence the price by their own actions. As a result, the individual firm is a price taker, accepting the price set by the market.
All firms sell an identical, or homogeneous, product, so buyers have no reason to prefer one seller over another, and no firm can charge a higher price.
Firms are free to enter the industry when there are profits and to leave when there are losses. This ensures that in the long run firms earn only normal profit.
Buyers and sellers have full knowledge of prices and conditions, and factors of production can move freely.

answer: Because of these features, a single price prevails and each firm faces a horizontal demand curve.
